Rafael / team — quick pass from me. Inline comments in the attached file (kim_copy_edits.docx) but summarized below:

1) Billing descriptor (one-liner) — recommend: "REDWOOD INF RNTL" (this follows AWS's guidance to keep it <= 22 chars, alphanumeric and spaces). If Acme wants the buyer-facing company name, we can use "ACME ANALYTICS / REDWOOD" but that may exceed some processors.

2) Product page copy edits — high priority:
- Replace the sentence "low cost per token" with a concrete savings statement tied to batching/quantization: "Lower per-token inference cost through automated batching and quantization profiles."
- Move the co-sell blurb into its own short section titled "Field enablement" and include one-sentence usage examples (3 bullets max) — this makes it easier for AWS field to scan.
- Trial CTA: change "Start a free trial" to "Request a 14-day trial instance" so we control provisioning and can tie it to entitlements.

3) Co-sell eligibility notes — to maximize co-sell opportunities include:
- Short customer use cases with outcome metrics (e.g., "reduced inference latency by 40% for real-time search").
- A one-page sales play with buyer personas attached (Marissa, can you add a link?).
- Confirm that the private offer terms contain the SLA and data residency checkbox if Acme needs EU coverage.

4) AMI/SKU naming (quick flag) — Jonas to confirm technical tags; note to AWS: we should include marketplace:ami=true and seller-id tagging.

I'll attach my edited doc. Happy to hop on a 20-min sync if needed.

—Kimberly
Director, Go-to-Market Content
Redwood Inference
